title: Keep the shop catalog local on Android
summary: The Android phone owns its catalog; Room and structured search serve the small offline inventory.
alternatives: Hosted multi-phone synchronization: deferred until the single-phone app proves useful in the shop.
Embeddings or a vector database: deferred until search misses demonstrate a need.
consequences: Local lookup works without an internet connection, but the owner must back up the phone and other devices do not sync.
context: The initial shop needs fast price lookup for roughly 500–1,000 items on one Android phone, including sizes and Hindi aliases.
choice: Use Kotlin/Compose with Room, Unicode FTS4, aliases and typo matching. Keep prices as integer paise on variants and use versioned ZIP backups.

title: Use OpenAI only behind explicit review and key boundaries
summary: Language understanding is online and produces suggestions; confirmed catalog changes remain local.
alternatives: Let AI directly update the database: rejected because incorrect prices or dimensions could be silently stored.
Bundle the development key in the APK or browser JavaScript: rejected because it exposes the credential.
consequences: Natural entry needs internet and a configured key. Manual entry and local search remain available without either.
context: Natural Hindi/English entry can misread sizes, prices or selling units, and the user chose OpenAI instead of the provider in the original plan.
choice: Use the Responses API with strict JSON schemas. Send parsed items to an editable review and require confirmation before saving. Store phone keys in Android Keystore and keep the localhost development key server-side.

title: Keep the web build as a separate local preview
summary: The browser version is a quick way to inspect the interface and workflows, with its own data.
alternatives: Build shared cloud storage and Android/browser synchronization now: outside the requested preview scope.
Serve the repository directory directly: rejected because local configuration and credentials must not be exposed.
consequences: Android ZIP and browser JSON backups are separate formats, and users must not assume the catalogs synchronize.
context: After the Android build, the user asked for a localhost web version to quickly look around.
choice: Use a dependency-free Node server and HTML/CSS/JS frontend on loopback. Persist the preview catalog in browser IndexedDB and reuse the Android AI prompts/schemas.

title: Share one workflow and keep project memory in the repository
summary: Codex and Claude Code use the same instructions and skill; the project history stays readable without either tool.
alternatives: Maintain independent Codex and Claude instruction copies: avoided because their rules and context would drift.
Use chat transcripts or an external project service as the only memory: avoided because they are harder to skim and would require extra accounts or tool access.
consequences: Both agents can use the same local workflow, but instructions guide behavior rather than enforce it. Agents must actually log meaningful completed work and keep the snapshot current.
The journal helper uses a POSIX file lock on Mac/Linux; Windows checkouts need a compatible environment and care with the skill symlink.
context: The user wants project-specific guidance for multiple coding agents and an easy way to revisit completed work, architecture and decisions.
choice: Keep AGENTS.md as the shared instructions, import it from CLAUDE.md and link Claude’s skill path to the canonical .agents skill. Store append-only outcomes and ADRs in docs/events.jsonl, maintain the current snapshot in docs/project.json and render Markdown plus a read-only localhost cockpit.

title: Route image entry and AI categories through editable review
summary: Product photos, labels and lists can be cropped locally and understood by AI, with editable item/category suggestions before any catalog write.
alternatives: Upload the original image as soon as it is selected or save recognized items automatically: rejected because users need control of both the submitted region and catalog changes.
consequences: Image recognition and category suggestions need internet and an API key. Manual entry, local cropping and local search remain available offline. Real-world recognition still requires user review.
context: The user wants to add items from images, crop them and have AI intelligently categorize products.
choice: Crop, position, zoom and rotate locally. Send only the accepted crop with an explicit Review items or Suggest category action, using Responses vision inputs and strict schemas. Missing prices remain blank; category and alias suggestions update drafts only. A single-item input can supply its product photo.

title: Use discounts as a one-time selling-price calculator
summary: An optional percentage computes the price to save; existing storage and backups continue to hold one selling price per size and unit.
alternatives: Persist a base price and a recurring discount rule alongside each selling price: deferred because it adds pricing states and could accidentally reapply discounts.
consequences: No database migration or backup-format change is needed. Price history records actual net-price changes; the percentage itself is not retained as a separate pricing rule.
context: The user wants calculations such as 25% off while the product model retains one selling price per variant.
choice: Accept an optional 0–100% discount with up to two decimal places on item entry and quick price edit. Compute the rounded net amount in integer paise and save it as the selling price. Reopening an edit starts with the saved net amount and an empty discount field.

title: Added image entry, natural brand filters, AI categories and discount calculations
summary: Both Android and the local web preview support image-assisted item creation with cropping, natural brand/product filtering, editable AI categorization and one-time discounted selling prices.
changes: Added local crop/position/zoom/rotation controls for product photos and image-based listing, shared strict category schemas, and explicit image submission to OpenAI review.
Brand-aware offline filtering supports Prince only and sockets from Prince only, including plural item words and strict brand constraints during rewritten searches.
Entry and quick-price forms accept optional discount percentages, display the net selling price, save integer paise and show actual last-price-update dates. Local Android build version is 0.2.0.
checks: 17 Kotlin unit tests, 11 Android emulator tests and 17 web tests passed; Android lint reported zero errors.
The emulator verified crop/rotate/zoom output pixels and saved dimensions, plus discount persistence and price history without compounding.

An isolated browser catalog passed live vision on a synthetic Prince socket label, category suggestions, image review/save, 25% discount, natural brand/product filters and quick-price editing. The existing localhost catalog was not changed by fixture writes.
next: Recognition quality on the owner’s real photos and real phone still needs shop validation. GitHub’s published APK remains 0.1.0; the new 0.2.0 APK is a local build.

title: Keep manufacturer references separate from carried shop variants
summary: The source PDF becomes an immutable reference library; only owner-reviewed variants with confirmed selling prices enter the shop catalog.
alternatives: Seed all source products into the shop catalog: rejected because it would imply availability and clutter counter searches.
Treat a supplier SKU or list rate as a unique shop product and selling price: rejected because codes repeat across source contexts and rate units vary.
consequences: The owner must choose carried variants and confirm specifications, selling units and prices. No quantity is created, and carried means a shop selection rather than a live stock count.
The original PDF and generated source page images stay local and Git-ignored; recreating those views on another checkout requires the source PDF and the documented import command.
context: The shop carries only part of a 92-page manufacturer pricelist. List rates, pack details and product codes do not prove stock or establish shop selling prices.
choice: Bundle a provenance-rich JSON library separately from Room and IndexedDB shop products. All reference variants start stock unconfirmed and hidden from shop search. Activation opens blank price and unit fields; saved variants retain unique stable source IDs. Preserve the PDF, source dates, printed headings and flagged anomalies. Android schema 2 migrates existing data; backup version 2 retains reference links and accepts legacy version 1.

Added individual variant selection and editable review with blank selling price/unit fields. Unique source IDs prevent repeated activation and survive editing, Room migration and version 2 backups; legacy version 1 restores remain supported.
Built a local 0.3.0 APK. Also fixed a renderer race where a recycled crop-preview bitmap could crash image rotation.
